How this repo builds classic eSignature (envelope) templates from its own agreement library, how the
tabs are placed and proved, and how a Workflow Builder (formerly Maestro) workflow carries and prefills one. Measured on the
legacy lab account in October 2026. Compiler: `src/esign-template-spec.ts`; documents:
`captures/esign-template-docs.ts`; proof: `captures/esign-template-verify.ts`; library:
`assets/esign-templates/specs/`.

## What one is made of

A spec names a **document template** of the library (`from`) and fixes a **variant**:

```json
{ "id": "mutual-nda-fontara-uk", "from": "mutual-nda",
  "variant": { "fontara_entity": "Fontara UK Ltd", "disclosure_period": "2 years", "confidentiality_period": "3 years" },
  "variantLabel": "Fontara UK Ltd",
  "owners": { "default": "Counterparty", "fields": { "effective": "Fontara", "purpose": "Fontara" } },
  "emailSubject": "Mutual NDA with Fontara UK Ltd" }
```

The compiler renders the document template's blocks to HTML. Then `esign-template-docs.ts` prints
that HTML to a **PDF**, committed as `assets/esign-templates/documents/<id>.pdf`. The compiler then
writes the eSignature REST template: the PDF, one signer role per document-template signer (in
routing order), and every tab.

- **A classic template is static.** A document template's conditional clauses and its dropdowns that
  print text are resolved by the variant at build time, and the variant goes in the name ("Mutual
  Non-Disclosure Agreement (Fontara UK Ltd)"). Every field a condition reads, and every dropdown,
  must be fixed. The compiler refuses otherwise, because a field left as a tab could be filled with a
  value the clause above it was not chosen for. Fixing the entity changes the text: the UK variant
  prints English law, the US one Delaware.
- **A signer the variant leaves out is not a recipient.** When every line of a role sits in rules the variant
  does not print, the template has no such role. So one document template gives one template per signer
  count: [`home-purchase-offer`](../assets/document-templates/specs/home-purchase-offer.json) puts the
  Co-Buyer's name and signature in rules on `buyers`; `home-purchase-offer-one-buyer` has Buyer and Seller,
  `home-purchase-offer-two-buyers` adds the Co-Buyer. A workflow picks one by the answer
  ([`home-purchase-offer-send`](../assets/workflows/specs/home-purchase-offer-send.json)). Verified 2026-11-01 on
  a second lab account: the one-buyer template read back with Buyer and Seller only, the two-buyer one with the
  Co-Buyer at routing 1 and its signature tabs placed; the workflow imported and drew clean (not run).
- **Every other field is a text tab, named by its KEY.** It belongs to the signer `owners` names
  (default: the first signer) and is unlocked, so a person sending the template by hand can still
  fill it. Two occurrences of a field are two tabs with one label, and so one value.
- **`radios`** shows a field as a radio group instead: `"radios": { "plan": ["Monthly", "Annual"] }`
  (field key → two or more options; also on each `documents[]` part). The group is named by the
  field's key, so a template-linked web form makes it a radio choice. Not for a field fixed in
  `variant` or owned by the sender; a workflow's Prepare step does not fill it. Proved 2026-10-31 on
  the lab account: gym-membership-agreement-loc01's four plan radios landed on their anchors, and the
  gym-membership-signup web form made `plan` a radio choice (webform-template-verify PASS).
- **Signature blocks** become Signature, Name, Date (+ Title, Company, Email). **Inline signer
  fields** (`[[initials:Role]]`, `[[check:…]]`, `[[radio:…]]`, `[[attach:…]]`, `[[text:…]]`,
  `[[email:…]]`, …) become their tabs. **Line items** become three rows of optional cells.
- **An `image` block** (`{ "image": "<repo path>", "align"? }`, PNG or JPEG under 1 MB) prints in the PDF as the
  image. The library's document template [`equipment-rental-agreement`](../assets/document-templates/specs/equipment-rental-agreement.json) carries the Fontara logo this way
  (commit d7132d38; see [DOCUMENT-TEMPLATE-SPEC.md](DOCUMENT-TEMPLATE-SPEC.md)).

## Several documents, copies, reminders, expiration, brand

These are envelope-level settings. The spec carries them; the compiler writes them as the REST API
stores them. Example: `assets/esign-templates/specs/customer-onboarding-packet.json`.

```json
{ "id": "customer-onboarding-packet", "from": "service-level-agreement", "variant": { … },
  "documents": [{ "from": "acceptable-use-policy", "variant": { "fontara_entity": "Fontara, Inc." }, "owners": { "default": "Customer" } }],
  "carbonCopies": [{ "role": "Fontara Legal" }],
  "reminders": { "delayDays": 2, "frequencyDays": 3 },
  "expiration": { "afterDays": 30, "warnDays": 5 },
  "brand": { "lock": true } }
```

- **`documents`**: more documents after the first. Each is a library document template at a fixed
  variant, built the same way (its own `owners`). Document n is printed to `<id>-<n>.pdf`. The signer
  roles are every document's signers, in order of first appearance. A role signs only the documents
  whose template names it.
- **Anchors are numbered across all documents.** eSignature searches every document of the envelope
  for an anchor, so `/e001/` in two documents would be one tab placed twice. Each tab names its
  `documentId`.
- **`carbonCopies`**: Receives a Copy roles (`recipients.carbonCopies`). Routing order defaults to
  after the last signer. A copy role may not also be a signer.
- **`reminders` / `expiration`**: `notification` with `useAccountDefaults: "false"`. The stored
  template has no `useAccountDefaults`, so the read-back compares only `reminders` and `expirations`.
  `warnDays` must be fewer than `afterDays`.
- **`brand`**: `{ name?, lock? }`. A brand id belongs to ONE account (`GET /brands`; another account's id is dropped
  silently on create, lab probe 2026-10-30), so the spec names no id. The template carries `brandLock`; the run that
  posts it (verify, deploy) resolves the brand on the target account (`resolveAccountRefs`): `name` by its exact name,
  no `name` = the account's sending default brand (`senderBrandIdDefault`). An account without it gets no brand setting,
  with a note in the report (testdiff, 2026-11-10: the lab account id did not travel). Signing groups resolve the
  same way: a missing group is created with `--create-signing-groups` (member: the account user; a verify names it
  `ZZ Lab · …` and deletes it), otherwise the role stays a plain recipient and the report says FLAGGED.

**Brands and reply-to on the account (lab, 2026-11-23).** What a template keeps, and what it does not:
- A template's own brand beats the account's default; a template with no brand, and an envelope with no `brandId`,
  get the sending default. Only a template GET shows its `brandId` (the template list does not).
- **A template keeps no reply-to.** `PUT /templates/{id}` with `emailSettings` answers 200 and stores nothing, and
  `POST /templates/{id}/email_settings` makes a new blank template. Reply-To is per envelope
  (`emailSettings.replyEmailAddressOverride` at send). So a spec carries no reply-to: put a contact address in the
  email text, or set it on each send. The From line stays "<user> via Docusign" whatever the brand.
- A brand is made with `POST /brands` and ONE brand object (a `{"brands": [...]}` body answers 400
  `BRAND_NAME_INVALID`); `isSendingDefault` / `isSigningDefault` make it the default, and `PUT /brands/{id}/logos/{primary|secondary|email}`
  takes the PNG bytes. Sender name and contact address go into the brand's email resource file
  (`PUT /brands/{id}/resources/email`, raw `text/xml`); the brand's `emailContent` refused every type tried.
- A web form's brand is set on the form by hand (form ▸ Settings ▸ Branding; the API refused it). Workflow Builder's
  Send step has no brand choice: the envelope gets its template's brand, or else the sending default.
- Use only a brand the customer gave you (their logo, their colours): never fetch a logo from the web.

The read-back gate and the upload gate both check these settings on the stored template. Proved on
the lab account with `customer-onboarding-packet` (2026-10-30): create, read back, a draft and Upload
Template keep both documents, the copy, reminders, expiration and the locked brand.

## Signing order and recipient authentication

- **`routingOrder`**: `{ "<role>": <n> }`, 1 first. Roles with the same number sign in parallel (the board's
  directors at 1, the secretary at 2). Roles not named keep their position. A copy's default order is
  after the highest signer order.
- **`auth`**: per signer role, `{ "accessCode": "…" }` (the sender gives the recipient the code) and/or
  `{ "idv": "IDV (Standard)" }` (Docusign ID Verification: `identityVerification.workflowId`). The IDV
  workflow ids are the ones `GET /identity_verification` lists on the lab account (Docusign's own
  workflows); that another account has the same ids is not checked, so IDV is a CONFIRM item on deploy.
  Phone authentication (SMS or a call) is `{ "idv": "Phone Auth", "phone"?: { "countryCode": "1", "number": "4155550100" } }`:
  the editor stores the number list with it and accepts an empty number (harvest 2026-11-01; not yet verified).
- **`delivery`**: per signer role, `{ "via": "sms" | "whatsapp", "phone"?: { "countryCode": "1", "number": "4155550100" } }`:
  the role gets its signing link by text message or WhatsApp (`deliveryMethod` `SMS` / `WhatsApp`, `phoneNumber`).
  Without `number` the sender types the phone at send. Needs SMS / WhatsApp delivery on the account (on for
  the lab account). Proven 2026-11-04 (library spec `volunteer-waiver-sms`: stored, uploaded and drafted as written; nothing sent).
- A workflow's Send step sets its own order and does not read the template's (`src/workflow-spec.ts`).
- **A role that fills fields signs no later than the others.** In sequence, a signer before it would sign with
  those fields blank, unless they are prefilled at send (a workflow's Prepare step fills and locks them), which
  the template cannot know. So the compiler WARNS (`warnings`, printed by `esign-template-docs.ts` and kept in the
  verify report). With one such role the fix is to route it first, unless the role's signature attests to the
  others' (the board consent: the secretary certifies that every director signed, so the secretary signs LAST and the
  officer, the effective date and the resolutions are sender prefill fields, `owners: { "default": "sender" }`; a
  `lineItems` table follows the owner of its `name`, as a field would). When
  several roles fill fields (an NDA's Fontara terms and the counterparty's address), someone signs first: the
  sender or the workflow prefills.
- **Names fit in 100 characters.** Upload Template keeps the first 100 (lab 2026-10-30: the upload gate then found no
  template by its full name). So the compiler shortens a longer name, prefix included, at a word boundary with "…"
  (`fitName`, `src/names.ts`) and warns; give the spec a shorter `name` to choose the words. A solution refuses a
  bundle whose prefixed name is still over its kind's limit.

## Recipient types, messages, conditional fields, more tabs (proved by `residency-affidavit`, 2026-10-30)

Spec: [`residency-affidavit`](../assets/esign-templates/specs/residency-affidavit.json). It passes all seven gates on the lab account, Upload Template included.

```json
"inPerson": ["Affiant"],
"witnesses": { "Witness": "Affiant" },
"viewers": [{ "role": "Records Office" }],
"messages": { "Witness": { "note": "…", "subject": "…", "body": "…", "language": "es" } },
"conditional": { "Previous address": { "parent": "Less than one year at this address", "value": "on" } }
```

- `inPerson` moves a signer role to `inPersonSigners` (the sender hosts; the host is named at send).
  `witnesses` moves a role to `witnesses` with `witnessFor` = the witnessed signer's recipient id. `viewers`
  are Needs to View recipients (`certifiedDeliveries`), after every signer unless given an order.
- `messages`: per recipient a private `note` and/or its own `emailNotification` (subject, body,
  `supportedLanguage`).
- `conditional`: the child tab gets `conditionalParentLabel` / `conditionalParentValue` (a checkbox parent's
  value is `on`; a radio group or dropdown parent's is one of its options). **Stored, the parent label is
  prefixed with the parent tab's id**: `##parent<tabId>##<label>`.
- New signer fields in a document's text: `[[number:Role:Label]]`, `[[list:Role:Label:A|B|C]]` (a dropdown),
  `[[ssn:Role:Label]]`, `[[zip:Role:Label]]`, `[[stamp:Role:Label]]` (a signature tab with `stampType:
  "stamp"`, for a company seal).
- **A phone tab is a notary tab.** `phoneNumberTabs` was refused on a signer, an in-person signer and a
  witness: `NOTARY_INVALID_NOTARY_TABS_ONLY_ALLOWED_FOR_NOTARY`. So `[[phone:…]]` is refused; use a text tab.
- The verifier compares witnesses, in-person signers, viewers, messages and conditional fields, and counts the
  tabs of every recipient that carries tabs.
- In a workflow, the Send step addresses the template's **signers** only. Runs on a second lab account
  (2026-10-31, [live report](../assets/workflows/live/send-envelope-viewer-run.json)):
  - A template with an **in-person signer or a witness** cannot be sent from a workflow. The drawer cannot name
    those roles, and the run fails to create the envelope: 400 `INVALID_USERNAME_FOR_RECIPIENT` "'name' not set
    for recipient". The compiler refuses such a template in a `sign`.
  - A **viewer** (Needs to View) is listed by the drawer and imports, but the run's envelope leaves it out (two
    runs, both the `preparedTemplates` and the builder's `unifiedDocuments` shape). The compiler refuses a viewer
    role. Re-test with the Send step redesign (2026-11-05) on
    [`residency-declaration`](../assets/esign-templates/specs/residency-declaration.json): a resident signs
    remotely and the Records Office views (all verify gates pass on a second lab account).

## More tab settings (proved by `supply-order-acknowledgment` and `residency-affidavit`, 2026-10-30)

Specs: [`supply-order-acknowledgment`](../assets/esign-templates/specs/supply-order-acknowledgment.json) (field-token options, formula tab, signing order off, locked field)
and [`residency-affidavit`](../assets/esign-templates/specs/residency-affidavit.json) (two witnesses). Both pass all seven gates on the lab account.

- **Options on a field token**, after its label, `;`-separated: `[[text:Customer:PO number:width=160;pattern=^PO-\d{6}$;message=Use PO-123456;tooltip=Your purchase order number]]`
  → `width`, `validationPattern`, `validationMessage`, `tooltip` (also `maxLength=N`, `conceal`, and `locked`: the
  sender or a workflow fills it, the signer cannot change it). An unknown option is refused (it used to be ignored
  silently).
- **`formulas`**: `{ "Total": { "formula": "[Quantity] * 25", "decimals": 2 } }`, placed by `[[calc:Role:Total]]`;
  every `[Label]` must be a number tab.
- **`[[prefill:Label]]`** (no role): a sender prefill field. It goes on the document (`documents[].tabs.prefillTabs.textTabs`),
  not on a recipient; the sender types it before sending. Read back with `GET /templates/{id}/documents/{n}/tabs`;
  Upload Template keeps it (verify 2026-10-31). `supply-order-acknowledgment` has one (Ship-to warehouse).
  A `{{field}}` becomes one when its owner is `"sender"` (`owners.fields`), labelled by the field key; the
  closing-package corpus template makes its loan terms sender prefill fields on all 12 documents (31 tabs,
  stored and uploaded). Whether same-label prefill fields share one value while preparing is not checked.
- **`signingGroups`**: `{ "Finance Approver": "Finance Approvers" }` — the role goes to a signing group, any one
  member signs. A group is an account object (Settings ▸ Signing Groups): the compile writes `signingGroupName`, and
  every deploy and verify calls `resolveSigningGroups` (GET /signing_groups) to write its `signingGroupId` before
  POST /templates; a name the account lacks is an error. Prerequisite for `vendor-payment-release`: the group
  "Finance Approvers" (the lab account has it as "Fontara Finance Approvers", id 1840368, from before the library went company-agnostic on 2026-11-23: a verify there uses `--create-signing-groups`, which makes a ZZ Lab group for the run). The verify draft keeps the group (no name or
  email for that role) and checks its members came with it. Workflow Builder forces email-only delivery for a group.
  To make a group by API: `POST /signing_groups` with `groupType: "sharedSigningGroup"` on each group. Without it the
  call still answers 201, with "Invalid group type" in each group's `errorDetails`: read the body (lab, 2026-11-06).
  Name groups by role ("Finance Approvers", "Legal"), never with the company name.
- **`signingOrder: false`**: every signer at routing order 1 (all at once). `supply-order-acknowledgment` has it.
  The warning about a role that fills fields (above) does not fire: nobody signs before anyone else. With
  `routingOrder` too, the spec is refused (the two keys say two things).
- **`tabWidths`**: tab widths in points, by tab label (`{ "Title": 216 }`). A signature block's Title tab has
  Docusign's default width, too narrow for a long job title; 216pt nearly spans the 225pt signing rule and fits
  "Customer Success Manager, UK & Europe". `ai-acceptable-use-acknowledgment` has it.
- **`lockedFields`**: field keys whose tabs are locked; the sender or a workflow fills them, no signer can change
  them (the draft gate prefilled a locked tab).
- **Two witnesses for one signer** (`witnesses: { "Witness": "Affiant", "Witness 2": "Affiant" }`) store and
  upload as written.

## Custom fields, more recipient types, approve/decline/note, checkbox groups, tab order (compiled 2026-11-02, live proof queued)

Library specs [`vendor-onboarding-routing`](../assets/esign-templates/specs/vendor-onboarding-routing.json) and
[`purchase-request-approval`](../assets/esign-templates/specs/purchase-request-approval.json) carry them; each row stays
compiled-unproven until its verify report is committed.

| Spec | Template JSON | Read back by |
|---|---|---|
| `customFields: [{ name, options?, value?, required?, show? }]` | `customFields.textCustomFields` / `listCustomFields` (a list when `options`); value ≤ 100 characters | readBack `customFields`; gate `accountCustomFields`: the account's Envelope Custom Fields list is unchanged |
| `recipientDefaults: { <role>: { name, email } }` | the signer's `name` / `email` | readBack `defaults` |
| `editors` / `agents` / `intermediaries: [{ role, routingOrder }]` | `recipients.editors` (Allow to Edit), `agents` (Specify Recipients), `intermediaries` (Update Recipients); ids after the copies and viewers | readBack `others` |
| `notary: { role, for: [<signer role>…] }` | `recipients.notaries` (one notary, id after the other roles, routing order of the first `for` role); each `for` signer gets `notaryId`. Stored on the lab account (probe 2026-11-09). Sending needs Docusign Notary and a notary user (deploy-preflight need `notary`); a workflow's Send step refuses the template. Electronic seals and an EU qualified signature type are not compiled: that account has no seal (`SEAL_INVALID_NAME`) and no qualified provider (`SIGNATURE_PROVIDER_INVALID_NAME`) | readBack `notaries` |
| `documentVisibility: true` | `enforceSignerVisibility`: each signer sees only the documents with their tabs (proven 2026-11-10, `customer-onboarding-packet-private`). Not compiled: `allowMarkup` (the lab account refuses a draft with it: CANNOT_ALLOW_MARKUP) and a template password | readBack `envelopeOptions` |
| `[[approve:Role:Text]]`, `[[decline:Role:Text]]` | `approveTabs` / `declineTabs`, `buttonText` = the text | tab count, placement |
| `[[note:Role:Text]]` | `noteTabs` with `value` = the text | readBack `notes` |
| `[[check:Role:Label:group=<name>;min=1;max=2]]` (the document template syntax) | each box `tabGroupLabels: [<name>]`, not required; one `tabGroups` entry per role and group (`SelectAtLeast` / `SelectAtMost` / `SelectExactly` / `SelectARange`) | readBack `tabGroups`, `groupMembers` |
| `[[address:Role]]` (one per role) | a verified postal address: five blanks (Address Line 1, City, State, Zip Code, Country or Region) placed as the editor's Address (DV) group — four `textTabs` and a country `listTabs` (240 countries) with tab labels `com.docusign.extensibilityplatform.action.verify.postaladdress@1.0.0.VerifyPostalAddressInput[0].<part>`, `mergeFieldXml` and `extensionData` for the account's Smarty app (assets/esign-templates/data-verification.json; harvest B10-6, the lab account 2026-11-04). Needs Smarty installed. A Phone Number (DV) group needs a phone verification app, which the lab account lacks | proven 2026-11-04 (B10-6b, address-change-verified) |
| `tabOrder: true` | each anchored tab's `tabOrder` = its anchor's number (top to bottom) | readBack `tabOrder` |

The verifier also compares `description` and `shared` (every template), and its values gate now checks that EVERY tab
of a field holds the value (a field printed twice; report key `replicated`).

Not compiled, and why: notary tabs (a notary places them in the session); smart
sections (responsive signing on an HTML document; ours are PDFs); comment threads (made by recipients while signing,
not on a template); view tabs (need supplemental documents [inferred]); a template password
(property name not harvested).

## Account settings a template needs (`src/esign-account-settings.ts`, 2026-11-10)

A library template that works on one account can be refused, or saved without a feature, on an account with an
eSignature account setting off. The compiled template carries its needs (`accountSettings`, read off the template:
a witness, a tab order, a notary role…). Before the create, `esign-template-verify` and `deploy-scenario --solution`
read the account's settings (`GET /settings?include_metadata=true`, read-only) and print one line per need:

- on;
- `CAN TURN ON` — the metadata says `rights: editable`: an account admin can, and `--enable-account-settings` (a Test
  account only) does it, one PUT per setting, the account's name checked before each, ledgered (`kind: account-setting`
  in captures/esign-template-api/LEDGER.jsonl; `account-settings` in the deploy ledger; park leaves them);
- `NEEDS DOCUSIGN` — `rights: read_only` (an Account Plan Editor item) or an add-on: what to ask for.

A need marked `blocks` (seen to break the template when off) skips the template with that message, not a failure;
`--settings-only` prints the plans and stops. Others are listed and turned on, but the template still deploys.

| Need | Setting (GET /settings) | Who can turn it on | Admin path / what to ask for | Blocks |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Document visibility (`documentVisibility: true`) | `documentVisibility` (Off → `SenderCanSetMustSignToViewUnlessSenderAccount`) | admin, API | Sending Settings ▸ Document Visibility | yes: Off stored `enforceSignerVisibility` false |
| Tab order (`tabOrder: true`) | `tabAccountSettings.allowTabOrder` | Docusign (read_only) | Account Plan Editor "Allow Tab Order" | yes: every `tabOrder` dropped |
| Notary role (`notary`) | the sender's `GET /current_user/notary` profile | Docusign | Docusign Notary add-on (`allowRemoteNotary` and the `allowOrganizationToUse…Notary` settings are read_only) and a notary profile | yes: `POST /envelopes` 400 `notary_api_resource_not_found_or_access_denied` |
| ID Verification (`auth.idv`) | the workflow in `identityVerification` | Docusign | the ID Verification module | yes |
| Witnesses | `enableWitnessing` | admin, API | Sending Settings ▸ Allow senders to add witnesses | no: saved and drafted with it off |
| SMS / WhatsApp delivery | `allowSMSDelivery`, `allowWhatsAppDelivery` | admin, API (where the plan has the module) | Sending Settings ▸ SMS / WhatsApp delivery | no |
| Signer attachments | `enableSignerAttachments` | admin, API | Sending Settings ▸ Allow signers to add attachments | no |
| Signing groups | `allowSigningGroups` | admin, API | Signing Groups | no |
| In person, Needs to View, Specify / Update Recipients, Allow to Edit | `allowInPerson`, `sendToCertifiedDeliveryEnabled`, `enableSendToAgent`, `enableSendToIntermediary`, `enableSendToManage` | admin, API | Sending Settings ▸ recipient roles | no |
| Calculated, conditional, approve/decline, note fields, regex validation | `enableCalculatedFields`, `conditionalFieldsEnabled`, `tabAccountSettings.approveDeclineTabsEnabled`, `noteTabsEnabled`, `dataFieldRegexEnabled` | admin, API | Sending Settings ▸ fields and properties | no |

Rights as read on 'Test (different account settings)' (testdiff) with claude@ (an admin). Not in the library, so not
checked: conditional routing (`allowAdvancedRecipientRoutingConditional`, read_only) and comments
(`commentsAllowEnvelopeOverride`, editable). Proof (testdiff, 2026-11-10):
document visibility turned on → `customer-onboarding-packet-private` PASS; witnesses turned on → `residency-affidavit`
PASS; `purchase-request-approval` and `residency-affidavit-notarized` SKIP with the Account Plan Editor / Notary message.

Turning settings on: send one `PUT /settings` with only the editable settings that are off, then read them back. A
setting can read back as off right after the PUT (`enableWitnessing` read `false`, then `true` a moment later; lab,
2026-11-23), so read again before you report a failure.

## Header and footer on every page (`header`, `footer`)

```json
"header": "Declaration of Residence, form RD-1",
"footer": "Page {page} of {pages}"
```

Plain text printed in the top and bottom page margin of every page of every document (the PDF printer's header and
footer, `src/esign-template-pdf.ts`); `{page}` and `{pages}` print the page number and the page count. Use it for a form
version or a consent version on every page (corpus example `hc-clinical-trial-consent`). The text is part of the PDF, so
the stored template carries it: `esign-template-verify` reads the stored document back and checks both lines on every
page (gate `headerFooter`; proved by [`residency-declaration`](../assets/esign-templates/specs/residency-declaration.json)
on a second lab account, 2026-10-31). A library document template's own Word `header` / `footer` is not used here.

## eSignature for Salesforce envelope templates (`salesforce`)

The Salesforce package (eSignature for Salesforce, namespace `dfsle`) stores an envelope template as records:
`dfsle__EnvelopeConfiguration__c` with child `dfsle__EnvelopeConfigurationRecipient__c` (and
`…Document__c`, `dfsle__CustomRecipient__c`). Their fields and JSON shapes were read from the org's two saved
templates through the account's Docusign Salesforce connection (connected-data search, read-only, 2026-10-30).

Spec: [`mutual-nda-salesforce`](../assets/esign-templates/specs/mutual-nda-salesforce.json). Status: **proven by sends from a record** (2026-10-31): the configuration and its related-list recipient lookup ([report](../assets/esign-templates/live/mutual-nda-salesforce-send.json)); merge fields and the custom button ([report](../assets/esign-templates/live/mutual-nda-salesforce-button-merge.json)). Recipients from a lookup field of the source object: **proven by a send from a CPQ Quote** (2026-10-31, [`mutual-nda-quote-salesforce`](../assets/esign-templates/specs/mutual-nda-quote-salesforce.json), [report](../assets/esign-templates/live/mutual-nda-quote-salesforce-send.json)).

```json
"salesforce": {
  "sourceObject": "Opportunity",
  "recipients": {
    "Counterparty": { "relationship": "OpportunityContactRoles", "relatesTo": "OpportunityContactRole", "filter": "Role = 'Decision Maker' AND IsPrimary = true" },
    "Fontara": { "sender": true }
  },
  "onCompleted": { "Opportunity.NextStep": "Mutual NDA signed — schedule discovery" },
  "writeBack": { "nameFormat": "Name", "includeCertificateOfCompletion": true },
  "mergeFields": { "counterparty": { "path": "Opportunity.Account.Name" }, "purpose": { "path": "Opportunity.Name", "editable": true } },
  "button": { "label": "Send Mutual NDA" }
}
```

- A recipient from a **lookup field** of the source object: `{ "lookup": "<relationship name>", "relatesTo": "Contact" | "User" | "Lead", "label"? }`,
  e.g. on the CPQ Quote `"Counterparty": { "lookup": "SBQQ__PrimaryContact__r", "relatesTo": "Contact", "label": "Primary Contact" }`
  and `"Fontara": { "lookup": "Owner", "relatesTo": "User" }`. The wizard (Add Recipient ▸ Lookup Fields) saved exactly
  `Relationship__c: { relatesTo: ["Contact"], name: "SBQQ__PrimaryContact__r", label: "Primary Contact", isLookup: true }` with no
  filter (harvest 2026-10-31). Sent from a ZZ Lab quote, the sending page filled the quote's Primary Contact and its Owner.
  The wizard lists only the source object's OWN lookups to a person: a person behind another record (Account ▸ Owner)
  is not offered, so a dotted `lookup` is refused. Use the record's own Owner, or a related list, instead.
- `mergeFields`: a text tab (by field key) filled from the source record when sent from Salesforce. Stored on the
  eSignature template's tab as `mergeField: { configurationType: "salesforce", path, writeBack, allowSenderToEdit }`
  (the account stores the path lower-cased). `writeBack: true` writes the signer's value back on completion (not run).
- `onSent` / `onCompleted`: field updates on the source record when the envelope is sent / completed, stored in
  `Options__c` as `envelopeEventUpdates: { sent: { "Opportunity.StageName": "…" }, completed: { … } }` (the same shape as the
  org's own configuration). **Run-proven 2026-11-04** ([`mutual-nda-salesforce-field-updates`](../assets/esign-templates/specs/mutual-nda-salesforce-field-updates.json),
  [report](../assets/esign-templates/live/mutual-nda-salesforce-field-updates-send.json)): one approved send from a ZZ Lab
  Opportunity moved its Stage to Negotiation/Review about a minute after the send, and to Closed Won once both signers signed.
  The library spec now writes the Opportunity's Next Step instead ('Mutual NDA out for signature', then 'Mutual NDA signed — schedule discovery'): no sales
  team closes a deal on an NDA, so the Stage stays the sales team's (2026-11-15; the Next Step write is not re-run yet).
  A draft fires neither: the update comes with the envelope's sent and completed status events.
- `button`: the custom button that sends it, a `WebLink` on the source object (`salesforceButton`), deployed with the
  Metadata API. The deploy does not add it to the page layout; a person does.

`salesforceEnvelopeConfig(spec, compiled, { docusignTemplateId })` returns the sObject Tree request
(`POST /services/data/vXX.X/composite/tree/dfsle__EnvelopeConfiguration__c`): the configuration (`SourceObject__c`,
`DocuSignId__c` = the deployed eSignature template, `Action__c: Prepare`, email subject and message,
`Notifications__c` JSON from the spec's reminders and expiration, `Options__c` JSON with `envelopeEventUpdates`
{sent, completed} and `documentWriteBack`) and one recipient record per signer role: a related list
(`Relationship__c` JSON + `Filter__c` JSON) or the sender (`IsSender__c`, `IncrementRoutingOrder__c`). The documents
come from the eSignature template, so no document records are written. Every signer role must say where it comes from.

Lab, 2026-10-30 (`mutual-nda-salesforce`, ZZ Lab, the lab account + the Developer Edition org): the template was created
by REST, the tree inserted (201, configuration + 2 recipients), read back through the Docusign connection with every
field as written, and listed under Docusign Envelope Templates; then deleted by id and the template recycled.
**Inserted without `IsDraft__c`, a configuration is a draft** (it defaults to true); the compiler writes `false`, as
the org's saved ones. Since then `captures/deploy-scenario.ts --solution` creates the template and inserts the tree
(`src/salesforce-rest.ts`), and `park-scenario` deletes the records by id (2026-10-30, [UPLOAD-GUIDES.md](UPLOAD-GUIDES.md#salesforce-envelope-templates)).

**Send from a record, 2026-10-31** (the lab account and the Developer Edition org; ZZ Lab Account, Opportunity and
Contact as the primary 'Decision Maker' contact role). The eSignature for Salesforce sending page loaded the configuration:
- Documents: the configuration's eSignature template.
- Recipients: Counterparty = the ZZ Lab contact (the related-list lookup and its filter); Fontara = the sending user.
- The email subject and message came from the configuration.
- Prepare & Send made a draft envelope (custom field `##SFSource` = the opportunity). It was not sent: the draft was
  recycled and its `dfsle__Envelope__c` rows deleted.

The sending page opens only from a **custom button**. Opened directly, `/apex/dfsle__sending` answers "This page
requires a CSRF confirmation token". The template wizard's button is a `WebLink` on the source object. The org's
button reads:
`{!URLFOR($Site.BaseUrl + '/apex/dfsle__sending', null, [sId = Opportunity.Id, sendingExperience = 'null', isEmbedded = false, templateId = '<configuration id>', recordId = Opportunity.Id, title = '<label>'])}`
(display type button, link type url, open in the same window). Creating one through the Tooling API
(`POST /tooling/sobjects/WebLink` with `Metadata`) failed with JSON_PARSER_ERROR on every string value; the Metadata
API deploy (`POST /services/data/v62.0/metadata/deployRequest`, `package.xml` + `objects/<Object>.object` with one
`webLinks` entry) works, and a destructive deploy deletes it.

**Merge fields and the button, 2026-10-31** (deploy-scenario with `mergeFields` and `button`): the button's link
opened the sending page with no CSRF error, and the draft's tabs read the opportunity's account name and the
opportunity name. park-scenario deleted the button, the records and the template.

## A new document, written inline

`from` (and `documents[].from`) takes a library document template id **or a new document inline**, in the
same shape as a document template spec: `{ "name", "fields", "signers", "body", "examples"? }`. It is
rendered and tabbed exactly like a library one (same blocks, `{{field}}` slots, `[[kind:Role:Label]]`
signer fields, `{ "sign": Role }` blocks, same static rules). So a solution can write the customer's own
agreement without adding it to the document template library. Example:
`assets/esign-templates/specs/field-trip-permission.json`.

- The library commits each template's PDFs (`npx tsx captures/esign-template-docs.ts <id>`). A project
  (a solution's folder) keeps its own templates in `<dir>/esign-templates/specs/` and prints their PDFs beside
  them with `--root <dir>`; `setEsignRoots([<dir>])` makes `compileEsignTemplate` read there before the
  library. To print at build time instead: `printEsignDocuments(c.documents.map((d) => d.html))`
  (`src/esign-template-pdf.ts`, headless Chromium), then `buildEsignTemplate(spec, { pdfs })`.
- **Without Playwright** (the Claude skills): `printEsignPdfs(<project>)` (`src/esign-template-print.ts`) prints each
  missing PDF with the machine's own Chrome or Chromium (`--headless --print-to-pdf`; `$CHROME` names the binary) and
  writes the HTML beside it. The HTML carries its page size and margins, so the result tabs the same way: the corpus
  answer `legal-litigation-settlement` printed so has the same page count, all 17 anchors, and the same template JSON
  apart from the PDF bytes (test/esign-template-print.test.ts). **Live 2026-10-31** (the lab account, `--root`):
  that Chrome-printed template passed every gate, Upload Template and placement on the uploaded copy included, with IDV
  on the Plaintiff and both counsel at routing order 3 as written; report and tagging-view pictures in
  `assets/prompt-corpus/live/settlement-signature-pages*`.
- A workflow's `esign` step refuses a template with `carbonCopies`: the Send step addresses the template's
  signer roles only, so a copy role would go out unaddressed. Use the sign step's `copies` instead.

## Envelope shares (`share`)

`share: [{ "with": "<email>", "permission": "view" | "edit" | "manage", "message"? }]` (at most 100) shares every envelope
sent from the template with colleagues, through the eSignature EnvelopeShares API (v2.1). The colleague sees that one
envelope (Agreements, and `GET /envelopes/shared` on their own sign-in) without being a recipient and without Shared
Access to the sender's other envelopes. A share is not part of the template: the compile writes the
`POST /envelopes/{envelopeId}/shares` body (`envelopeShares`; in a solution bundle `esign-template-<id>.envelope-shares.json`),
sent after each send. `resolveShareUsers` replaces each email with the user's `userId` and `accountId`.

Probe, Test 2 (a second lab account) 2026-11-05, ledgered:
- A share by email alone: 400 `INVALID_USERID` ("Expected a valid guid"). The API takes the user by id.
- An invited user (`ActivationSent`): 400 `USER_LACKS_MEMBERSHIP`. The colleague must be an ACTIVE user of the account.
- `GET /envelopes/shared` as the sender lists envelopes shared WITH the caller, not by them. With
  `X-DocuSign-Act-On-Behalf` it answers 401 `ACT_ON_BEHALF_USER_NOT_ALLOWED`.

Library spec [`mutual-nda-shared-with-legal`](../assets/esign-templates/specs/mutual-nda-shared-with-legal.json). Live gate
`share`: `DS_ACCOUNT=test2 npx tsx captures/esign-template-verify.ts <spec> --send-share --share-with=<an active zz-lab user>`
sends one envelope to zz-lab inboxes, shares it with that user, reads the shares back, deletes them and voids the envelope.
**Proven 2026-11-05** on Test 2 ([report](../assets/esign-templates/verify/mutual-nda-shared-with-legal.json)): every gate passed.
The colleague gets an email for each change: "Claude shared <subject> with you" and "Claude removed your access to <subject>".
A user added by API must activate first (the activation email in the lab inbox ▸ Create account ▸ set a password); the lab user
was closed after the run.

## Anchors

Every tab sits on its own white anchor token `/e001/`, `/e002/`, … — fixed width and terminated.
eSignature matches anchors as case-insensitive SUBSTRINGS, so no token may sit inside another.
Every tab is `anchorIgnoreIfNotPresent: "false"`. That makes the draft gate meaningful: an envelope
is created at all only if every anchor was found.

Offsets were measured in the draft's own tagging view, not copied:

| Where | Offset (points) | Why |
|---|---|---|
| A blank in running text | y −6, width = the blank (134; 242 when the example value is long) | its token sits at the blank's TOP; a signature-block offset put the tab a line high, over the text above |
| A rule in a signature block | y −16 | the token sits at the BOTTOM of the rule |
| Signature | y 0 | `src/forms.ts`'s −28 left the box 27pt above its rule |
| Checkbox, radio | x −4, y −1 | the tab sat 4pt right of the box |
| Attachment | y 0, in a 0.6in mark | a ~40pt tab hangs from the token at the mark's top |
| Initials | y +30, in a 0.6in mark | eSignature puts the box's bottom ~30pt below its top at the anchor (like a signature), so at y 0 it rose over the line above; reported by its box top, 30pt above the anchor (the placement gate allows for it). Measured 2026-11-01 |

A text tab GROWS to fit its value. So a field whose example value is longer than 24 characters gets a
wide blank, or a long agreement name would run over the words after it.

## The gates

`npx tsx captures/esign-template-verify.ts assets/esign-templates/specs/<id>.json --cdp` (the default account,
through the explore browser), or `DS_ACCOUNT=legacy …` without `--cdp` (the JWT client):

1. **validate** — the spec compiles.
2. **create** — `POST /templates` under a `ZZ Lab · ` name, ledgered before the call.
3. **read back** — every role, and the tab count per role.
4. **draft** — an envelope FROM the template, status `created` (never sent), every role addressed to
   the self address, every field prefilled with the document template's example value. Every tab
   must then have a page and a position.
5. **prefill** — every prefilled value is on its tab.
6. **upload** — the same JSON the gallery offers, under a lab name, through **Templates ▸ Start ▸
   Envelope Templates ▸ Upload Template** (the app posts it to `/api/send/upload-template/templates`).
   It must come back with its document and every tab.
7. **deleted** — the draft recycled, and every template moved to **Deleted Items** the way the UI
   deletes one (`PUT /folders/recyclebin {"envelopeIds":[templateId]}`, recorded off the UI). A GET on
   the exact id must then report `folderName: "Deleted Items"`. The bin is never emptied. A template has no
   DELETE: a recycled one still answers a GET (never a 404), so the folder is the proof.

Since 2026-10-31 two more gates: **placement** — every anchored tab of the draft is on the page of the PDF that prints
its anchor, at the anchor (`pdftotext -bbox`) plus its offset, within 10 points; a signature tab is reported by the top
of its box, 26 points above its anchor — and **uploadPlacement**, the same on a draft from the UPLOADED template, with
its own tagging-view pictures. `--root <project> --report-dir <dir>` verifies a project's own template (a corpus
answer's report goes in `assets/prompt-corpus/live/`).

The picture is the draft in eSignature's own **tagging view** (the embedded sender view: `POST
/envelopes/{id}/views/sender`, whose URL is a one-time credential and is never logged). It shows every
tab where it will be. The signature page is reached from the last thumbnail
(`[data-qa="indvidual-tagger-documents"]`).

## In a workflow

```json
{ "esign": "confidentiality-invention-assignment",
  "fill": { "effective": "new-employee-onboarding.start_date", "employee": "new-employee-onboarding.sign_name" } },
{ "sign": { "Employee": "New hire", "Fontara": "Fontara signatory" }, "subject": "…" }
```

- **The template travels.** The package carries an `eSign` component (`esign/<templateId>.json`: the
  template JSON with its `templateId`, as a real export carries an ADF one). Import creates a copy and
  points the step at it: the PDF-based template imported, rewired and drew clean (2026-10-24).
- **Prepare eSignature Template** (`PrepareESignTemplate` / `DS-SignPrepareESignTemplate`):
  `config: { templateId }`; `input.recipients.signers` lists each role, and a filled text tab carries
  `value` (the variable) and `locked: "true"`, as real exports do. Its output is
  `preparedEsignTemplate_<stepId>` (type `PreparedEsignTemplate`, `defaultValue: { templateId,
  brandLock: "false" }`). Saved: `{ tabs: { <tabId>: <the editor's document> }, templateId }`. That map is what
  the step's drawer shows (a mention of the variable, or plain text).
- **Tab positions, so the drawer shows the fills** (lab 2026-10-31,
  [live report](../assets/workflows/live/esign-drawer-fills.json)). An import gives the template new tabIds and
  re-keys the step's tabs and the drawer map. It does this only for a step tab whose `pageNumber`, `xPosition` and
  `yPosition` exactly match where the account places that anchored tab. `npx tsx captures/esign-tab-positions.ts
  <id> | --all [--root <bundle>]` creates each template in the lab and reads the placed tabs. It writes
  `esign-templates/positions/<id>.json` (keyed by role/label, stale when the template's documents or tabs change),
  then deletes the template. With that file the compiler gives each carried text and number tab a fixed tabId and
  those positions. Without it the drawer shows every fill empty: the run still fills them, but saving the drawer
  clears them all and unlocks every tab. `workflow:check` warns about that case.
- **Send Documents for Signature** then sends `preparedTemplates: [{ preparedTemplateMetadata: <that
  output> }]` with PLAIN recipient ids (`"1"`), where a generated document's are
  `<templateId>_<recipientId>`. Its saved state names `preparedEsignTemplate_<stepId>`.
- `fill` refuses a field the variant fixed (it has no tab), a checkbox group, and a non-text agent
  output. A date fills as the respondent typed it (`.userValue`).
- **Where a tab's value comes from.** A form answer, `start.<name>`, a text agent output, and two more
  (commit 848b9ee4; [docs/WORKFLOW-SPEC.md](WORKFLOW-SPEC.md), the `esign` row):
  - **A Read from Salesforce or lookup output**, `<as>.<field>`. The drawer's variable picker lists Read from
    Salesforce ▸ Opportunity / Name for a text tab. Example: [`aup-from-opportunity`](../assets/workflows/specs/aup-from-opportunity.json) fills the
    `acceptable-use-policy` template's `customer` from `opp.Account.Name` and `agreement` from `opp.Name`. Run
    2026-10-30: the envelope's customer tab read the value from Salesforce.
  - **A request field**, under a request start: a `C_…` field or `TicketTitle`. Example:
    [`aup-on-sales-contract-request`](../assets/workflows/specs/aup-on-sales-contract-request.json) fills `customer` from `C_CounterpartySigner` and `agreement` from
    `TicketTitle`. Run 2026-10-30: the envelope's tabs held the request field and the request title.
  - Both workflows pass verify (import, rewire, canvas, review) on the legacy account (commit e2536234).
- **A Send step addresses the template's signers only** (`recipients.signers`). A `sign` that maps a viewer
  (Needs to View), agent, editor, intermediary or copy role of the template is refused, and the message names the
  role's kind: make the role a signer on the template, or send the template outside the workflow. A template with
  an in-person signer or witness role is refused in a `sign` even when the step does not map it: the run cannot
  create the envelope. Rows `workflow.step-setting.send-envelope-nonsigner-roles` and
  `workflow.step-setting.send-envelope-inperson-witness` are refused (runs 2026-10-31, see
  [Recipient types](#recipient-types-messages-conditional-fields-more-tabs-proved-by-residency-affidavit-2026-10-30)).
- `workflow-verify.ts` diffs the account's eSignature templates around the import, checks the step,
  the Send step and the saved state all name the NEW copy, and recycles it.

## Payment tab, PowerForms, bulk send (lab probes, the lab account, 2026-10-30)

Spec keys (proved by [`camp-registration`](../assets/esign-templates/specs/camp-registration.json), all gates plus `powerForm`):

```json
"payment": { "role": "Parent or Guardian", "item": "Camp deposit", "amount": 250, "description": "…", "currency": "USD", "gatewayAccountId": "<the account's>" },
"powerForm": { "signingMode": "direct", "instructions": "…", "maxUses": 300 }
```

- `payment` adds a last page to the first document: the amount is a locked number tab on an anchor
  (`PaymentAmount`), the payment is a formula tab `[PaymentAmount]` with `paymentDetails`, placed by POSITION
  under "Pay here:" (page = the PDF's page count). With no `gatewayAccountId` the compiler writes a zero GUID and
  warns: the target account's gateway must be set at deploy.
- `"amount": "per-envelope"` (proved by [`membership-dues-payment`](../assets/esign-templates/specs/membership-dues-payment.json),
  2026-10-31: a draft made with 125.50 kept it on the locked tab, the payment tab read it, and the tagging view showed
  "$125.50 USD" on the payment page; no send, as the account has no payment gateway) leaves `PaymentAmount` locked and EMPTY: the sender fills it for each envelope — in the send
  flow, in the API's `templateRoles` (`numberTabs: [{ tabLabel: "PaymentAmount", value }]`), or in a bulk list's
  `<payer>::PaymentAmount` column, or a workflow's `esign` step: `"fill": { "PaymentAmount": "<form>.<currency or
  number field>" }` (the Prepare eSignature Template step writes it as the payer's number tab; corpus bundle
  `gov-permit-application`: staff set the fee on a form). The payer cannot change it. The verifier makes its
  draft with 125.50 and checks the tab (gate `paymentAmount`); `--send-payment` also sends it to zz-lab inboxes and
  voids it before anyone pays. Recurring or SEPA direct-debit payments: the product's payment tab is one
  charge, so `payment.recurring` / `frequency` / `installments` / `mandate` is refused, naming the workaround (one
  envelope per installment by Bulk Send, or a signed mandate form) (`esign-template.tab.payment-recurring`, a guard).
  Also refused as guards: `conditionalRouting` / `routingGroups` (Workflow Builder rejects routing groups: route in the
  workflow) and `transformPdfFields` / `pdfFormFields` (tabs come from anchors: Transform PDF Fields by hand).
- `"amount": { "formula": "[Balance] / [Installments]", "decimals": 2 }` (proved by corpus answer
  `fin-collections-payment-plan`, template `payment-plan-first-payment`, 2026-10-31, report
  [`assets/prompt-corpus/live/payment-plan-first-payment.json`](../assets/prompt-corpus/live/payment-plan-first-payment.json):
  the stored template kept the formula and the payment's line item, and a draft with Balance 1234.56 and Installments 6
  kept both; the draft's `PaymentAmount` reads empty, as a formula is computed while signing; no send, no gateway)
  computes the amount while signing. `PaymentAmount` becomes a locked formula tab (a calculated field) with that
  formula, and the payment tab still reads `[PaymentAmount]`, its line item `amountReference: "PaymentAmount"`. That
  is the shape of Docusign's own payment example (eg014: the payment formula `([l1e] + [l2e]) * 100` and the line
  items' `amountReference` name formula tabs). Each `[Label]` is a number tab of the PAYER (`[[number:Payer:Label]]`,
  usually with `;locked`): a calculated field reads its own recipient's fields. The formula is plain arithmetic:
  numbers, `[Label]`s, `+ - * /` and parentheses; `decimals` (default 2) rounds it. The sender fills those number
  tabs (send flow, API `numberTabs`, a bulk list's `<payer>::<label>` columns), or a workflow's `esign` step:
  `"fill": { "Balance": "<sf read>.Overdue_Balance__c", "Installments": "<form>.<field>" }` (written as the payer's
  number tabs, locked). The verifier's `paymentFormula` gate makes its draft with the example values on those tabs
  and checks the stored formula, the inputs and the payment's line item. A workflow cannot do the arithmetic itself
  (no arithmetic step), so the eSignature template does it.
- `powerForm` compiles to `compiled.powerForm`, the `POST /powerforms` body without `templateId` (the deployed
  template's). The verifier's `powerForm` gate creates it INACTIVE from the lab template, reads it back
  (signing mode, use limit, roles), deletes it and expects a 404.

The account has **no payment gateway** (`GET /payment_gateway_accounts` returns `{}`) and no PowerForms.

- **Payment tab.** `POST /templates` with a `formulaTabs` entry carrying `paymentDetails` (`gatewayAccountId`
  = a placeholder GUID, `currencyCode: "USD"`, `lineItems: [{ name, description, amountReference: "TripCost" }]`)
  and a `numberTabs` amount (`TripCost`), both placed by x/y, answered 201. The stored tab keeps `formula`,
  `lineItems` and `paymentOption: "authorize"` (with `status: "new"`); it **drops `gatewayAccountId` and
  `currencyCode` silently**. A draft envelope from it was created (status `created`, never sent) and carried the
  same `paymentDetails`. The same compiled template twice, the payment tab placed by **anchor** in one and by
  **x/y** in the other: the anchored one was stored **without any `paymentDetails`**, the positioned one kept them.
  So the compiler places the payment tab by position. A payment
  cannot be run on this account: a send needs the account's gateway (Settings ▸ Payments), so a payment
  template is a prerequisite item for the target account.
- **PowerForm.** `POST /powerforms` with `{ templateId, name, signingMode: "direct", isActive: "false",
  maxUseEnabled: "true", usesRemaining: "5", recipients: [{ roleName, recipientType: "signer", routingOrder }] }`
  answered 201 with `powerFormId` and `powerFormUrl` (`…/Member/PowerFormSigning.aspx?PowerFormId=…`). `GET
  /powerforms/{id}` read it back; `DELETE /powerforms/{id}` removed it, and a GET then answered 404
  `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND`. A PowerForm is an account object made FROM a template at deploy, not part of the template
  file.
- **Bulk send** is a send-time action (a recipient list, e.g. a CSV, applied to a template when sending), not a
  template setting; nothing in the template file models it. The compiler writes the LIST instead (next section).

## Bulk send (`bulkSend`)

`"bulkSend": true` (proved by [`field-trip-permission`](../assets/esign-templates/specs/field-trip-permission.json),
2026-10-31 on the lab account: two rows, two envelopes, each with its row's recipients and values, voided) makes the compile also write the bulk send list, `compiled.bulkSend` (`columns`, `csv`). A
solution bundle carries it as `NN-esign-template-<id>.bulk-send.csv` beside the template, with a README note and
the [Bulk send](UPLOAD-GUIDES.md#bulk-send) guide. A manifest can add it to a library template with
`"set": { "bulkSend": true }`.

The format is Docusign's (help, Bulk Send for Multiple Recipients: topics cfi1718042055824, tem1718212446511,
lao1578456383175, fjy1718143883386; its sample lists show `Approver::Name, Approver::Email, Approver::Language, …`):

| Column | For |
|---|---|
| `<role>::Name`, `<role>::Email` | every recipient role: signers, in-person signers, copies, viewers, in the template's order |
| `<role>::Host Name`, `<role>::Host Email` | an in-person signer's host |
| `<role>::<tab label>` | each field tab the role owns (the field KEY, so a workflow and a list fill the same tab) |
| `<role>::PaymentAmount` | a per-envelope payment |

- One row per envelope, at most 999 rows. The compile writes ONE example row: the document template's example
  values and `zz-lab.<role>-1@example.com` inboxes, to be replaced by the real list.
- Refused: a witness role (the help lists the recipient types a list takes: Needs to Sign, In-Person Signer,
  Receives a Copy, Needs to View, Specify/Update Recipients); a role name with `( ) : ; < > @`; a label with a
  comma or a period.
- With `auth`, the compiler warns: access codes and ID verification are list columns, not template settings (take
  them from Bulk send ▸ Upload a file ▸ **Sample File**).
- Docusign's own sample list also has `<role>::Signature Provider` (optional; the upload offers to accept it).
- The help's other columns are not written: `<role>::Language`, `<role>::Email Subject`, `<role>::Email Body`,
  `<role>::Note`, `ECF:<name>` (envelope custom fields), `<role>::Signature Provider`.
- **Proof** (`captures/esign-template-verify.ts --bulk-send`, gate `bulkSend`): the compiled header with two rows of
  fresh zz-lab inboxes (written beside the report as `<id>-bulk-send.csv`) is turned into a `POST /bulk_send_lists`
  body (`bulkSendList`, src/esign-bulk-send.ts: each `<role>::<label>` cell a recipient tab `{ tabLabel,
  initialValue }`) and sent from the lab template. Both envelopes are read back (each row's recipients and values),
  then voided, and the list is deleted.
- In the UI: Start ▸ Envelopes ▸ Use a Template ▸ Add recipients ▸ **Bulk send** ▸ Upload a file (captured:
  `gallery/agreements/02c-bulk-send-add-recipients.png`). Agreements ▸ **Bulk Send** lists the batches.

## Observed in the lab (2026-10-24)

- **A draft's PDF prints no tab value.** None of eight prefilled values appeared in a draft's
  downloaded text. They are flattened only when someone signs, so the prefill gate reads the tabs.
- **A recycled template still answers a GET.** It reports the Deleted Items folder, and the template
  list no longer finds it. Read the folder, not the absence.
- **The overlay of reported tab positions matched the tagging view for text tabs.** For a signature
  tab only the tagging view is the truth.
